summary: Level-2 fresh-context evaluation of PR #70 (AWS provider, F008 P4). Both SHAs re-derived with git ls-remote at start AND end of the evaluation; neither moved. All ten builder claims were INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED with the repository's own parser and classifier (evaluator-authored probes, not the PR's tests) and all ten matched. The headline result is genuine: AWS Step Functions is evidenced as `always_free` by a verbatim block of its own AND is still Z1_BILLING_EXPOSURE because the same page states overage is charged. The zero-Z0 outcome is a MEASUREMENT, proven non-vacuous by direct mutation: with the classifier's Z0 gate broken the positive control FAILS while the no-AWS-offer-reaches-Z0 sweep still passes, so the control is load-bearing rather than decorative. Five further evaluator mutations (card gate, automatic_billing gate, deleted/reworded/duplicated pinned blocks) all produced the required rejections with exact reasons (assertion_not_found, ambiguous_assertion), and a false-positive control confirmed the guards discriminate rather than reject any edit. Full suite reproduced at 2089 passed / 2 skipped against a dedicated PostgreSQL 16, and 1864 / 227 with DATABASE_URL unset. Protected state verified byte-identical BY BLOB/TREE HASH. .secrets.baseline growth fully accounted for: all 49 new entries are SHA-256 digests in committed AWS fixture captures, and the six sha256_stored values were recomputed against the committed bytes and match. No real credential and no internal package-feed hostname anywhere in the diff. The one red CI job (Dependency audit, GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8) is identical on main and unattributable: apps/web is byte-identical to base at tree 5e5024079d4a18e614bbe022545f7efd373331d4.

claims_rederived.claim: 3. The zero is a measurement, not a vacuous pass: a positive control returns Z0_TRUE_FREE and is genuinely non-vacuous.
claims_rederived.result: CONFIRMED BY MUTATION -- the strongest result of this evaluation
claims_rederived.measured: MUTATION A: patched apps/api/app/classify/engine.py gate 6 to return UNKNOWN instead of Z0_TRUE_FREE (patched line printed). test_the_z0_sweep_is_not_vacuous FAILED with "assert 'UNKNOWN' == 'Z0_TRUE_FREE'", while test_no_aws_offer_can_reach_z0 STILL PASSED (6 passed). This proves BOTH halves: the sweep alone is vacuous, and the positive control is the thing that rescues it. engine.py restored and verified at blob 900d27399040968774456a565ca4e1ddd2f1666b.

claims_rederived.claim: 4. Step Functions is genuinely always_free ('available to both existing and new AWS customers indefinitely') and still Z1 because the same page says 'You are charged per state transition above the free tier'.
claims_rederived.measured: Both quotes exist as EXACT whole-block matches in the committed capture, each occurring exactly ONCE with zero partial/superset matches, so neither is composed or paraphrased. The Z1 verdict does NOT rest on a hand-set field: MUTATION D deleted the 'charged per state transition' block -> error='assertion_not_found', offer_type=None (8 tests failed); MUTATION E reworded 'indefinitely' to 'for a while' -> error='assertion_not_found' (7 failed); MUTATION C disabled the engine's BILLING_EXHAUSTION branch -> tests failed. So removing the evidence REJECTS the document rather than leaving a perpetual offer looking unconditionally free.

claims_rederived.claim: 5. requires_card=True is quoted, not composed, from a block that names the free plan itself.
claims_rederived.measured: The pinned block is exactly: 'Yes, you are required to provide a valid payment method to sign up for an AWS account, whether you choose a free plan or a paid plan.' -- one exact whole-block match, zero supersets. It contains 'free plan' as well as 'paid plan', so it is NOT a paid-plan sentence generalised. MUTATION F reworded it to 'when you choose a paid plan.' -> error='assertion_not_found' (6 failed). MUTATION B disabled the engine's requires_card branch -> 3 failed. Adversarial sweep of all six profiles found ZERO requires_card=False and ZERO has_paid_dependencies=False assertions, columns or matrix rows: no AWS profile claims a card is NOT required, and only the FAQ profile asserts requires_card at all.

disclosed_errors_verified.error: (1) First concluded AWS never states an Always Free offer in its own block -- wrong in the omission-favouring direction; correcting it produced the sixth source.
disclosed_errors_verified.evidence: Six sources exist including aws-step-functions-free-tier, whose page states perpetuity in a block of its own; the profile emits offer_type='always_free' pinned to that block. The module docstring records the error verbatim ('That conclusion was wrong, and it was wrong in the favourable-to-omission direction'). This is the correct direction of self-correction under the product rule: a wrongly-omitted free offer is also a defect.

security_review.finding: CLEAN. All 49 new entries are type 'Hex High Entropy String' and every one is a SHA-256 digest: 11 sha256_stored, 6 sha256_original, and the remainder elements of asserted_block_sha256 arrays. No 'Secret Keyword', no Basic Auth, no key material. The baseline stores only hashed_secret / line_number / type -- no plaintext -- and no entry is marked is_secret=true. The 'it is just fixtures' explanation was NOT accepted on its word: all six sha256_stored values were recomputed from the committed source.html bytes and matched, proving these are content digests. 4107 added diff lines scanned against 11 credential-shape patterns (AWS AKIA/ASIA keys, AWS secret keys, GitHub/Slack/Google tokens, private-key blocks, JWTs, Azure storage keys, bearer literals, password/secret assignments, URLs with inline credentials): ZERO matches. Zero internal package-feed hostname leaks.

undisclosed_findings.finding: capture.json uses TWO different counting conventions for pinned blocks within the same file. structure.asserted_block_sha256 is per-ASSERTION (so it repeats a hash when several fields pin the same block: Step Functions has 7 entries for 4 distinct blocks), while live_reconciliation counts DISTINCT blocks ('all 4 pinned block(s)'). Both are internally consistent and the reconciliation figure is the correct one, but a reader comparing the two fields can easily mis-read the array length as the number of pinned blocks. Not a correctness defect and not blocking; worth a naming clarification in a later slice.

test_no_aws_offer_can_reach_z0 is, in isolation, a vacuous test -- this evaluator demonstrated it passes unchanged against a classifier that can never emit Z0. This is NOT a defect because the builder shipped exactly the control that fixes it, but it is worth recording explicitly that the control is load-bearing and must never be deleted as redundant.

No new instance of the known project-level gaps was introduced. sha256_stored still attests committed bytes only and each capture says so; the flattened-capture convention is unchanged; the in-cell p/li latent parser gap is untouched because five of six profiles read no table at all and the sixth's target table has no in-cell block elements.

evaluator_errors: Counted FIVE duplicated blocks in the 12-month Terms fixture and briefly treated the builder's 'four' as an under-count. WRONG: my probe ignored assertion SCOPE. 'AWS Free Tier Terms' appears once as title scope and once as heading scope, which are different scopes and cannot collide as an assertion. The document-scope duplicate count is four. The builder was right; I was wrong.

My first PowerShell mutation script aborted mid-run on an argument-quoting bug ('-k unfavourable or card' passed as one token) and, because the failure occurred before the restore line, left apps/api/app/classify/engine.py PATCHED on disk. I caught it on the next run only because I had a blob-hash PRE-check, then hard-restored with git checkout and re-verified against the committed blob. This is precisely the class of trap the brief warned about, and it is the reason the rewritten battery restores in a finally block. No mutated state reached any report or commit.

Read coverage provenance from a 'source_id' attribute when the config field is 'source', which briefly produced a false reading that the three offered_no_z0 rows had no provenance. Re-read from the YAML: all three declare a source. My probe error, not a defect.
Assumed tests/conftest.py and bs4 existed; neither does. The suite has no root conftest and the parser is stdlib html.parser. Cost one wasted probe each; no effect on findings.

method.independence: Every material claim was re-derived with evaluator-authored probes driving the repository's own _DocumentCollector, HtmlDocAdapter, resolve_profile, revalidate_quotas and classify. The PR's own tests were used only as mutation TARGETS (to observe whether they fail when the thing they guard is broken), never as the source of a pass.
method.database: dedicated postgres:16-alpine container, isolated port, fresh venv, alembic upgrade head
method.live_fetching: none; CI performs zero socket operations by design and no live fetch was attempted inside the suite
method.restoration_discipline: every mutation restored in a finally block and verified by git hash-object against git rev-parse HEAD:<path>, never by git diff --numstat

boundary.note: Read-only with respect to stsyg-ingest-aws-provider-profiles. Findings written only to the evaluator's own branch.

recommendation: PASS. Merge is justified on the evidence. F008 remains passes:false -- this slice is P4 of a six-provider feature and the ledger flag belongs to the epic close-out, not to this increment.
